evaluator_role: formats literal subquestions, routes Qwen text, detects missing/equal/disagreeing terminal fields, parses Qwen outputs, and scores/audits; all memberships, counts, sorted lists, and final comparisons are generated by Qwen
exact_rule: At r=0.9 each candidate likelihood is proportional to 9^m; at r=0.1 it is proportional to 9^(3-m). With four candidates per side, the first unequal entry of the descending (r=0.9) or ascending (r=0.1) Qwen-sorted count lists exactly determines the larger likelihood sum because 9 exceeds the maximum list width 4.

input_contract.evidence: the original three raw displayed sets and noisy YES/NO reports
input_contract.forbidden: no evaluator-derived memberships, match counts, sorted lists, likelihoods, posterior values, target-derived summaries, or learned readouts

prompt_templates.atomic_membership: Inspect the literal set in this single membership question. Is the integer {candidate} an element of {set}? Reply with exactly YES or NO.
prompt_templates.final: Prior Qwen stages produced sorted FIRST={first} and sorted SECOND={second}. Compare left to right. At the first unequal position, the side with the {larger_or_smaller} integer has the larger total likelihood; if all positions match, totals tie. A=FIRST, B=SECOND, C=tie. End with FINAL: A, B, or C.
prompt_templates.natural_order_visible_count: Compare the two words inside each bracket. For each Q write SAME if truth and report are identical, otherwise DIFFERENT. Then count the SAME labels. {Q1,Q2,Q3 Qwen-truth/report pairs in natural order}. End with COUNT: 0/1/2/3.
prompt_templates.sort: These four match counts were generated by prior Qwen stages: {counts}. Sort all four integers in {direction} order, preserving duplicates. End with SORTED {side}: followed by four actual digits.

scope: half-set probes at r=0.1 and r=0.9 only; multi-call Qwen self-computation

selection_history.reason_for_disabling_count_order_counter: On development repeats 0-1, natural-order Qwen counts were 98.4375% internally consistent, reverse-order counts 95.3125%, and disagreement adjudication systematically propagated several reverse-order mistakes. Natural order improved final decisions from 31/32 to 32/32.

status: selected on development repeats 0-3; validated unchanged on repeats 8-11; evaluated once on test repeats 12-15
